name: ITC Ltd.
business_summary: Diversified Indian conglomerate. Cigarettes are the profit engine (roughly three-quarters or more of segment EBIT, model knowledge, approximate), with a growing FMCG-others portfolio (Aashirvaad atta/spices, Sunfeast biscuits, Bingo, Yippee noodles, Classmate, personal care), paperboard/paper/packaging, and agri-business (leaf tobacco, wheat, spices, soya exports). Hotels were demerged into ITC Hotels (listed Jan 2025). Near debt-free, ~5% dividend yield. Since the 1 Feb 2026 shift to a higher excise-based tobacco tax regime (model knowledge on regime; Q1/Q2 FY27 reports confirm sharp profit damage) ITC has taken repeated price hikes and is trading volume against margin.

cost_structure.note: Excise/taxes on cigarettes are netted from net revenue; pass-through is the key variable

exposures.mechanism: Cigarettes ~75% of EBIT (approx). A further +10% tax burden/stick: ITC passes ~70% via price, volume falls ~3-4% plus mix/illicit shift, cigarette EBIT about -6%; x0.75 share = group EBIT -4.5%; structural so persistence 1.0; EV/MCap ~0.97 => about -5. Q2 FY27 shows the realised version: screener operating margin 28% vs 34% a year earlier, PAT -18.5%.

evidence.note: Reuters headline: ITC Q2 profit down ~20% as higher prices dent demand; screener Sep-26 qtr PAT 4,229 cr vs 5,187 cr
New Indian Express: tax hikes hit ITC, Q1 profit -27%

exposures.mechanism: FMCG-others (~25% revenue, ~11% EBIT approx) and agri (atta, spices) are rural-sensitive; cigarettes less so. +5pp rural growth => FMCG-others sales +2%, EBIT +4%, group EBIT +0.6%, plus cigarette volume uplift in rural/semi-urban ~+0.5pp => group EBITDA about +2.9% ; persistence 0.5; EV/MCap 0.97 => ~+1.4.

evidence.note: Moneycontrol: weak monsoon pressures rural demand ahead of festive season

exposures.mechanism: Premium cigarettes, hotels-linked brand halo, urban packaged foods. +5pp urban growth => cigarette volumes +1%, FMCG-others +3% => group EBITDA +2%; persistence 0.5 => ~+1.0.

evidence.note: FMCG segment growth at 14-quarter high per Q2 coverage (NiftyTrader 2026-11-03)

exposures.mechanism: Wheat ~8% of costs (atta, biscuits, noodles). +10% => costs +0.8% on the FMCG part (~35% of group costs) => group costs +0.3%, EBITDA -0.45% at 32% margin; 50% passthrough, persistence 0.5 => -0.1; agri trading/procurement benefits offset. Empirical +0.54 (t=1.0) has opposite sign, consistent with the agri offset; net kept small and sign-uncertain.

Palm/oil used in biscuits, snacks, noodles (~3% of group costs). +10% => costs +0.3% => EBITDA -0.5%; 50% passthrough, persistence 0.5 => -0.12; agri-business edible-oil trading marginal. Rounded to -0.3 for packaged-food-wide cost creep.

evidence.note: Reuters: India cuts edible oil import duty (lower oil prices help food makers)

exposures.mechanism: Packaging (BOPP/laminates, cartons) ~6% of costs for FMCG; ITC's own paperboard arm benefits from higher packaging prices (partial natural hedge). +10% => costs +0.6% => EBITDA -1.2%, 50% passthrough, hedge 40% => -0.35 after persistence 0.5.

evidence.note: Paperboard/packaging segment recovery noted in Q2 coverage (Kalkine 2026-11-04)

exposures.mechanism: Fuel (paperboard mills, logistics), BOPP and polymer packaging ~4% of costs linked to crude. +10% Brent => costs +0.25%, EBITDA -0.4%; persistence 0.5, EV/MCap 0.97 => ~-0.2, widened to -0.5 to include logistics and sentiment. Brent is +15% over 3m (94.99).

Agri exports (~15% of revenue, ~USD-linked) and leaf-tobacco exports gain from a weaker rupee; imports (pulp, packaging inputs, some cigarette materials) offset. Net ~ +1.4% EBITDA per +3% INR weakness => persistence 0.5 => ~+0.7; empirical +2.04 (t=2.1) larger; blended to +1.0 with range reflecting disagreement.
Cash-rich, dividend-yield stock (5.2%), P/E 18.5; no funding cost. +25bp repo => required equity yield up; defensive-high-dividend duration ~12 => -0.6 after partial offset by inflows to defensives.
FIIs hold 33.2% (down from 34.8% in Mar-26); GQG sold 2.91% in a Rs 9,395 cr block on 8 Oct 2026. +US$5bn/quarter inflow => liquid index heavyweight +1.2 (index-weight beta effect).

evidence.note: Upstox/Moneycontrol: GQG sells 2.91% of ITC for Rs 9,395 crore

exposures.mechanism: GST Council 8 Oct 2026 widened input-tax-credit scope (stock +5% intraday on 9 Oct). A further broad rate cut would lift FMCG-others/hotel-adjacent demand; cigarettes sit in the highest slab/excise regime and gain nothing. FMCG-others ~15% of group EBITDA: +3% sales and +6% EBIT => group +0.9%.

evidence.note: Outlook Money: Colgate, ITC rally as GST Council proposes easing ITC rules

exposures.mechanism: Stronger enforcement against illicit/low-tax cigarettes (CEO Sanjiv Puri flagged illicit-trade risk, Storyboard18 2026-08-27) would return volume to legal players; a theme proxy. +1 => legal volume +1.5% => cigarette EBIT +2% => group +1.5% x persistence 0.5.

evidence.note: Storyboard18: Puri backs FSSAI scrutiny, flags illicit-trade risk after tax hike
